title: The open-stabilizer submodule is right adjoint to the forgetful functor
statement: Let $G$ be a topological group and $R$ a ring. Let $\mathcal D_{R,G}$ be the category of left $R$-modules with an $R$-linear $G$-action whose elements have open stabilizer, and equivariant $R$-linear maps; let $\mathcal M_{R[G]}$ be the category of left $R[G]$-modules. The forgetful functor $v:\mathcal D_{R,G}\to\mathcal M_{R[G]}$ is fully faithful and carries monomorphisms to monomorphisms. It has a right adjoint $u$ sending an $R[G]$-module $M$ to the submodule $u(M)=\{x\in M\mid \operatorname{Stab}_G(x)\text{ is open}\}$, with the induced action. Injective objects are understood in the sense of [def-sp-injective-resolutions].

source.place: Tag 04JF, proof of lemma-G-modules, lines defining the forgetful functor v and its right adjoint u(M)

proof.text: The functor $v$ is fully faithful because a morphism in $\mathcal D_{R,G}$ is, by definition, exactly an $R$-linear map commuting with the $G$-action, hence exactly an $R[G]$-linear map between the underlying modules. Let $f:N\to N'$ be a monomorphism of $\mathcal D_{R,G}$ and $K$ the kernel of the underlying $R$-linear map. $K$ is an $R$-submodule of $N$, $G$-stable because $f$ is equivariant, and each of its elements has open stabilizer as an element of $N$; so $K$ with the restricted action is an object of $\mathcal D_{R,G}$ and the inclusion $i:K\to N$ is a morphism of $\mathcal D_{R,G}$. Then $f \circ i = 0 = f \circ 0$, so $i = 0$ and $K = 0$: the underlying map of $f$ is injective. An injective $R[G]$-linear map is a monomorphism of $\mathcal M_{R[G]}$ (if $v(f) \circ a = v(f) \circ b$ then $v(f) \circ (a-b) = 0$, so $a = b$), hence $v(f)$ is a monomorphism.

source.place: Tag 04JF, proof of lemma-G-modules, definition of v

proof.text: For an $R[G]$-module $M$, the set $u(M)=\{x\in M\mid \operatorname{Stab}_G(x)\text{ is open}\}$ is an $R$-submodule: the stabilizer of $x+y$ contains the intersection of the stabilizers of $x$ and $y$, and the stabilizer of $r x$ contains the stabilizer of $x$ because the action is $R$-linear. It is $G$-stable since $\operatorname{Stab}_G(gx)=g\operatorname{Stab}_G(x)g^{-1}$, so it inherits an $R[G]$-action and is an object of $\mathcal D_{R,G}$.

source.place: Tag 04JF, proof of lemma-G-modules, verification that u(M) is the open-stabilizer submodule

proof.text: For every $N\in\mathcal D_{R,G}$ and $M\in\mathcal M_{R[G]}$, an $R[G]$-linear map $vN\to M$ has image in $u(M)$, since each element of $N$ has open stabilizer and equivariance carries that stabilizer into the stabilizer of its image. Thus restriction and inclusion give mutually inverse, natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{R[G]}(vN,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D_{R,G}}(N,uM)$. These bijections exhibit $u$ as the right adjoint of $v$.
